judgments.yea_description: Voted to send S.J.Res. 13 to the President, using the Congressional Review Act to repeal the EEOC rule that required the commission to hand employers the factual and legal basis for a discrimination finding before settlement talks. It passed the House 219-210.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against sending S.J.Res. 13 to the President, which used the Congressional Review Act to repeal the EEOC rule that required the commission to hand employers the factual and legal basis for a discrimination finding before settlement talks. It passed the House 219-210.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.R. 239, the Equal Access to Contraception for Veterans Act, which barred the Department of Veterans Affairs from charging veterans copays for contraceptives that private insurance must cover for free. It passed the House 245-181.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against passing H.R. 239, the Equal Access to Contraception for Veterans Act, which barred the Department of Veterans Affairs from charging veterans copays for contraceptives that private insurance must cover for free. It passed the House 245-181.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to send S.J.Res. 14 to the President, using the Congressional Review Act to repeal the 2020 EPA rule that had removed methane emission limits from new and modified oil and gas sources, restoring those standards. It passed the House 229-191.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against sending S.J.Res. 14 to the President, which used the Congressional Review Act to repeal the 2020 EPA rule that had removed methane emission limits from new and modified oil and gas sources, restoring those standards. It passed the House 229-191.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.R. 2662, the Inspector General Independence and Empowerment Act, which limited the President's power to remove inspectors general, required reasons be given to Congress, and strengthened their subpoena and reporting authority. It passed the House 221-182.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against passing H.R. 2662, the Inspector General Independence and Empowerment Act, which limited the President's power to remove inspectors general, required reasons be given to Congress, and strengthened their subpoena and reporting authority. It passed the House 221-182.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.R. 2668, the Consumer Protection and Recovery Act, which restored the Federal Trade Commission's power to go to court for refunds and restitution from companies engaged in fraud, false advertising, or anticompetitive conduct. It passed the House 221-205.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against passing H.R. 2668, the Consumer Protection and Recovery Act, which restored the Federal Trade Commission's power to go to court for refunds and restitution from companies engaged in fraud, false advertising, or anticompetitive conduct. It passed the House 221-205.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.R. 2467, the PFAS Action Act, which directed the EPA to regulate PFAS forever chemicals as hazardous substances, set drinking water limits, and fund cleanup of contaminated sites. It passed the House 241-183.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against passing H.R. 2467, the PFAS Action Act, which directed the EPA to regulate PFAS forever chemicals as hazardous substances, set drinking water limits, and fund cleanup of contaminated sites. It passed the House 241-183.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.R. 3684, the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, which put roughly $1 trillion into roads, bridges, rail, transit, broadband, ports, airports, water systems, and the power grid. It passed the Senate 69-30.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against passing H.R. 3684, the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, which put roughly $1 trillion into roads, bridges, rail, transit, broadband, ports, airports, water systems, and the power grid. It passed the Senate 69-30.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.R. 4, the John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act, which restored the requirement that states and localities with a record of discrimination get federal preclearance before changing voting practices. It passed the House 219-212.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against passing H.R. 4, the John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act, which restored the requirement that states and localities with a record of discrimination get federal preclearance before changing voting practices. It passed the House 219-212.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.R. 4350, the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2022, which set defense policy and authorized Department of Defense programs, military construction, and related national security activities. It passed the House 316-113.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against passing H.R. 4350, the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2022, which set defense policy and authorized Department of Defense programs, military construction, and related national security activities. It passed the House 316-113.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.R. 3755, the Women's Health Protection Act, which created a federal statutory right to provide and receive abortion care and barred state restrictions such as waiting periods, mandatory tests, and telemedicine bans. It passed the House 218-211.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against passing H.R. 3755, the Women's Health Protection Act, which created a federal statutory right to provide and receive abortion care and barred state restrictions such as waiting periods, mandatory tests, and telemedicine bans. It passed the House 218-211.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.R. 3110, the PUMP for Nursing Mothers Act, which extended the right to break time and a private space to express breast milk at work to salaried and other workers the existing law left out. It passed the House 276-149.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against passing H.R. 3110, the PUMP for Nursing Mothers Act, which extended the right to break time and a private space to express breast milk at work to salaried and other workers the existing law left out. It passed the House 276-149.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.R. 2119, the Family Violence Prevention and Services Improvement Act, which reauthorized and expanded federal funding for emergency shelters and support services for domestic violence victims through 2026. It passed the House 228-200.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against passing H.R. 2119, the Family Violence Prevention and Services Improvement Act, which reauthorized and expanded federal funding for emergency shelters and support services for domestic violence victims through 2026. It passed the House 228-200.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to send H.R. 3684, the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, to the President, agreeing to the Senate version that put roughly $1 trillion into roads, bridges, rail, transit, broadband, ports, airports, water systems, and the power grid. It passed the House 228-206.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against sending H.R. 3684, the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, to the President, which agreed to the Senate version that put roughly $1 trillion into roads, bridges, rail, transit, broadband, ports, airports, water systems, and the power grid. It passed the House 228-206.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass S. 610, the Protecting Medicare and American Farmers from Sequester Cuts Act, which delayed automatic Medicare payment cuts through March 2022 and eased other scheduled reductions. It passed the House 222-212.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against passing S. 610, the Protecting Medicare and American Farmers from Sequester Cuts Act, which delayed automatic Medicare payment cuts through March 2022 and eased other scheduled reductions. It passed the House 222-212.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.R. 5314, the Protecting Our Democracy Act, which tightened limits on presidential pardons and emergency powers, strengthened enforcement of congressional subpoenas, and added transparency requirements for the executive branch. It passed the House 220-208.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against passing H.R. 5314, the Protecting Our Democracy Act, which tightened limits on presidential pardons and emergency powers, strengthened enforcement of congressional subpoenas, and added transparency requirements for the executive branch. It passed the House 220-208.
